text: A1 cannot get human output: digest_raw always appends --format json after the caller's args.
evidence: P5 records it. The Design's Test helper adds digest_raw_as(ws, args, diff, format); digest_raw keeps json and calls it.

text: No escaping contract: C-quoted diff paths can hold \n, \t, \r (diff_parser.rs:140-142), which would split a line or forge a changed-roots: line.
evidence: Design 'Escaping': every interpolated string has each char::is_control replaced with its escape_default form, other characters unchanged. A3 adds a \n/\t case, with a mutation proof.

text: Assembly invariants (diagnostics after entries, --tests line separate and last, exit codes) have no targeted test.
evidence: A5 is a CLI case with a resolved entry, an unmatched file and --tests, exit 0, asserting the exact order. A1 asserts exit 2 for ambiguity alone. A3 (b) pins the trailing bytes with an entry. The dependencies prefix stays covered by cli_digest_query_dependencies.rs:192.

text: A1's mutation (drop the loop) also breaks A3, so it does not prove the call site is guarded.
evidence: A1's mutation is now the call-site one, format_digest_human(&entries, &[]) in digest_view. A3 stays green under it.

text: 'Candidates taken from the same run's JSON' cannot work: a human run prints no JSON.
evidence: A1 asserts the whole stdout literal with the #77 A4 candidates (ws:Cloud/src/posting.al, ws:src/posting.al), plus exit 2. A2 is a separate JSON invocation with identical inputs.

text: A4 leaned on a contains-based test, and the bytes around the new lines (blank line, trailing newline) were unstated.
evidence: P7 records today's bytes. The Design states that there is no blank line and each line ends in \n. A4 adds assert_eq! cases with and without entries. A3 (b) covers the case with entries.

text: The remedy wording should say what <folder> means.
evidence: It now reads 'pass --diff-root <folder> to read diff paths relative to <folder>'. Spec r2 (sol re-raise): the first rationale was false. The diagnostic arises only under the default git-top reading: an explicit root gives at most one reading (digest_cli.rs:311-317), and ambiguity needs two (:345). The neutral wording stays because either reading may be the one meant.

text: Stale references: run_digest should be digest_view, P4's candidates were wrong, the unit-test line was wrong, and the CHANGELOG did not name the harm.
evidence: P1 and the Design name digest_view (:2090/:2180). P4 quotes the real candidates and exit code. The unit test is :2545-2558. The CHANGELOG names a run that exits 0 while a file goes unresolved.

text: The hunk line's numbers: the JSON casts i32 as u64 (:1566).
evidence: The HunkOutsideRoutines line uses the same 'as u64' values the JSON writes (P2 records the cast).

text: Query-level diagnostics (DIAG-digest-*) are also missing from human output; out of scope, so record it as a discovery.
evidence: Discovery D1 is in the ledger's ## Discoveries in the orchestrator's JSON shape; the Design's 'Not changed' names it.

text: char::is_control covers Cc only, so the bidi and line-breaking format characters (U+202E, U+2028, U+2029, …) from a C-quoted diff path print raw: a display spoof, or a line break in some viewers.
evidence: a0f1157d: escape_controls also escapes U+200E/F, U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069, U+2028/9 in escape_default form; the backslash stays as it is. A3 (a) adds a file holding U+202E and U+2028 that prints \u{202e}\u{2028}. Proof: dropping the check fails (a) and restoring it passes (ledger table).

text: The one-line guarantee covers only the changed-roots: lines; the entry block's strings are printed raw, so one document escapes some fields and not others.
evidence: a0f1157d: escape_controls' doc states its scope (the changed-roots: lines only; the entry block's evidence, detail and reasons print as before). The entry block is pre-existing output that #340's acceptance does not cover.

text: kind() is pub, but only this module calls it.
evidence: a0f1157d makes it private (grep: only digest_cli.rs calls it).

text: The CHANGELOG says the lines come after the entries; with no entries they come after 'digest: no changed roots resolved'.
evidence: a0f1157d states both placements and names the bidi/line-separator escaping.

text: Human output still drops the query-level diagnostics (DIAG-digest-root-not-in-snapshot, DIAG-digest-no-coverage-record), so a root that resolves and is then dropped still leaves no line.
evidence: Out of #340's acceptance, which names the changed-roots diagnostics. The ratified Design's 'Not changed' lists it, and the spec panel had it as S10. Filed as discovery D1 with its own acceptance.

text: Every non-AL file in a real diff (app.json, .xlf, .xml) becomes diff-file-unmatched, and the human output now prints a line for each, which is noise on ordinary runs.
evidence: Source-verified: diff_key turns every unreadable path into DiffFileUnmatched, and the parser has no .al filter. That classification predates #340; the JSON has always carried it, and #340 only makes the existing diagnostics visible as its acceptance asks. Changing what counts as unmatched is a changed-roots semantics change, filed as discovery D2 with its own acceptance.

text: hunk-outside-routines is emitted per hunk, so a table-field edit in 40 hunks prints about 40 lines; suggests grouping or a cap.
evidence: One line per diagnostic, in JSON order, is the ratified contract (Design 'Placement', A3). It mirrors the JSON array one to one, so a reader can match the two. Grouping would make the human output say less than the JSON. Each line names its file and range, which is what a reviewer needs.

text: With no separator after the last entry block, a run-level diagnostic reads as part of the last routine's block.
evidence: No blank line is the ratified choice (spec S6 and Design 'Placement', pinned by A3 (b)). The lines are not ambiguous: every line inside an entry block is indented two or four spaces (format_entries_human), while changed-roots: lines start at column 0 with their own prefix (see the six goldens).

text: escape_controls does not escape the backslash, so a literal '\n' in a path prints the same as an escaped newline.
evidence: The ratified contract is one line per diagnostic with no forgeable line (Design 'Escaping'), and that holds. Escaping '\' would double every separator of a Windows path the user passed (--file src\X.al), for the rare case of a literal backslash-n in an AL file name. G1's test pins that the backslash stays as it is.

text: The human hunk line copies the JSON's 'as u64' casts; a negative i32 would print as a huge number.
evidence: The cast was ratified in the spec panel (S9, raised by opus) so the human and JSON numbers agree. Negative values cannot occur: hunk lines come from the diff parser's eat_digits (diff_parser.rs:346), which reads digits only, and both outputs would show the same value anyway.

text: One line of the #340 CHANGELOG entry is 159 columns wide; its neighbours wrap at about 88.
evidence: ac041329 rewraps it to about 88 columns, the same text. A prose-only fix to a gate-inert file after H, closed by the raiser-only rule: opus raised it and accepts the rewrap, and sol's slot is accepted-by-rule.
